title: Hertha Berlin and Saarbrücken Face Off in the DFB Pokal
seoTitle: Hertha Berlin and Saarbrücken Face Off in DFB Pokal
subtitle: Match opens the cup season for both teams at the Ludwigspark Stadion.
excerpt: Hertha BSC and Saarbrücken prepare for a knockout clash in the DFB Pokal, marking the start of the cup season for both sides.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Hertha BSC is preparing to face Saarbrücken in a knockout match that marks the opening of the cup season for both teams. The clash brings together teams from different divisions, bringing expectations and uncertainties to the start of their competitive campaign.

Opening of the cup season

Ludwigspark Stadion hosts the match valid for the first round of the DFB Pokal. The duel brings together Saarbrücken, managed by Argirios Giannikis, and Hertha BSC, led by Stefan Leitl. Both teams underwent squad overhauls during the European summer, which adds uncertainty regarding team chemistry at this early stage.

Team performance and current situation

Saarbrücken approaches the clash with a solid foundation at home, having remained unbeaten in ten of their last twelve matches played at Ludwigspark Stadion. However, the coaching staff is dealing with physical issues that rule out important players from their attacking options, such as Patrick Schmidt and Christian Kühlwetter. On the other side, Hertha BSC carries recent fragility as a visitor, tallying four defeats in their last eight away games and averaging goals conceded per match.

Absences and defensive preparation

For the knockout duel, coach Stefan Leitl must deal with significant losses in his squad. Hertha BSC has players Bradley Ibrahim and Deyovaisio Zeefuik suspended, in addition to the injured J. Gottschalk. These absences leave the visiting team with fewer defensive alternatives to contain the opponent's strength on their home turf.

Market expectations and favoritism

The market points to Hertha BSC as the favorite for a win in regular time, reflecting the division difference between the clubs. However, Saarbrücken's home record and Hertha's away vulnerabilities make the game scenario balanced and unpredictable, especially considering it is a single-leg knockout format.
